questions.q: The price of an item is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net change?
If 25% of 200 equals 5% of x, what is x?
The population of a town is 8,000. It increases by 5% in the first year and decreases by 5% in the second year. What is the population after two years?
questions.exp: 8000 × 1.05 = 8400. Then 8400 × 0.95 = 7980. (Note: +5% then −5% always gives a net loss, never zero.)

questions.q: A number increased by 20% becomes 96. What was the number?
40 is what percent of 160?
If 15% of a number is 45, what is the number?
The price of rice rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family reduce consumption so that expenditure stays the same?
questions.exp: New price = 1.25 × old. To keep expenditure constant, quantity must be 1/1.25 = 0.80 of before → a 20% cut. Formula: r/(100+r) × 100 = 25/125 × 100 = 20%.

questions.q: In an exam, 35% of students failed in Mathematics, 25% failed in English and 10% failed in both. What percentage passed in both subjects?
questions.exp: Failed in at least one = 35 + 25 − 10 = 50%. Passed in both = 100 − 50 = 50%.

questions.q: A man buys an article for Tk 400 and sells it for Tk 500. What is his profit percentage?
An article is sold for Tk 720 at a loss of 10%. What was the cost price?
A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above cost price and then allows a 25% discount. What is his profit percentage?
questions.exp: Let CP = 100 → MP = 140. After 25% discount, SP = 140 × 0.75 = 105. Profit = 5 on CP 100 → 5%.

questions.q: Two successive discounts of 10% and 20% are equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.exp: Take MP = 100 → after 10% = 90 → after 20% = 72. Total discount = 28%. Shortcut: 10 + 20 − (10×20)/100 = 28%.

questions.q: The cost price of 20 articles equals the selling price of 16 articles. What is the profit percentage?
questions.exp: Let CP of each = Tk 1 → CP of 20 = Tk 20 = SP of 16 → SP of each = 20/16 = 1.25. Profit% = 0.25/1 × 100 = 25%.

questions.q: By selling an item at Tk 480, a trader loses 20%. At what price should he sell it to gain 20%?
After allowing a 20% discount, a shopkeeper sells a book for Tk 960. What was the marked price?
A trader sells an item for Tk 500 and makes a 25% profit on cost. What was the cost price?
If A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 7, then A : B : C = ?
questions.exp: Make the B term common. LCM of 4 and 6 = 12. A : B = 9 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 14 → A : B : C = 9 : 12 : 14.

questions.q: Tk 1,200 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. How much does C get?
The ages of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 7. After 8 years the ratio becomes 7 : 9. What is A's present age?
The average of 10 numbers is 25. If one number, 40, is removed, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.exp: Sum = 10 × 25 = 250. Remaining sum = 250 − 40 = 210 over 9 numbers. Average = 210/9 = 23.33.

questions.q: What is the average of the first 20 natural numbers?
The average of five consecutive odd numbers is 27. What is the largest of them?
questions.exp: For consecutive numbers the average is the middle term → the numbers are 23, 25, 27, 29, 31. Largest = 31.

questions.q: A batsman has an average of 40 after 10 innings. He scores 60 in the 11th innings. What is his new average?
questions.exp: Total after 10 = 400. After 11 innings = 460. New average = 460/11 = 41.82.

questions.q: A invests Tk 5,000 for 12 months and B invests Tk 6,000 for 10 months. What is the ratio of their profits?
A can do a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
A and B together can do a work in 6 days. A alone can do it in 10 days. How long will B alone take?
A can do a work in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 6 days. What fraction of the work is left?
questions.exp: Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12. Work in 6 days = 6/12 = 1/2. Remaining = 1/2.

questions.q: 10 men can complete a work in 15 days. They work for 5 days, then 5 men leave. In how many total days is the work completed?
questions.exp: Total work = 10 × 15 = 150 man-days. Done in first 5 days = 10 × 5 = 50 man-days. Remaining = 100. With 5 men: 100/5 = 20 more days. Total = 5 + 20 = 25 days.

questions.q: If 8 men can do a job in 12 days, how long will 6 men take?
A pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours and a drain can empty it in 9 hours. If both are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
A car travels 60 km at 40 km/h and another 60 km at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.exp: Time = 60/40 + 60/60 = 1.5 + 1 = 2.5 hours. Total distance = 120 km → 120/2.5 = 48 km/h. (Do **not** average 40 and 60 to get 50 — that is the classic trap.)

questions.q: A train 150 m long runs at 54 km/h. How long does it take to cross a pole?
A train 200 m long running at 72 km/h crosses a bridge 300 m long. How long does it take?
questions.exp: 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Total distance = 200 + 300 = 500 m. Time = 500/20 = 25 seconds.

questions.q: A boat goes 12 km/h downstream and 8 km/h upstream. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
Two trains, each 100 m long, run in opposite directions at 40 km/h and 50 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.exp: Relative speed = 40 + 50 = 90 km/h = 90 × 5/18 = 25 m/s. Total length = 200 m → 200/25 = 8 seconds.

questions.q: A man walking at 5 km/h reaches his office 10 minutes late. At 6 km/h he would reach 5 minutes early. How far is the office?

The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 9. If the digits are reversed, the new number is 27 more than the original. What is the original number?
questions.exp: Let the number be 10a + b, with a + b = 9. Reversed: 10b + a = 10a + b + 27 → 9b − 9a = 27 → b − a = 3. Solving: a = 3, b = 6 → 36. (Check: 63 − 36 = 27 ✓)

questions.q: The denominator of a fraction is 3 more than the numerator. If 2 is added to both, the fraction becomes 3/4. What is the fraction?
questions.exp: Let numerator = x, denominator = x + 3. (x + 2)/(x + 5) = 3/4 → 4x + 8 = 3x + 15 → x = 7. Fraction = 7/10. (Check: 9/12 = 3/4 ✓)

In a college of 100 students, 60% took Finance, 45% took Marketing and 45 students took Operations. 10 students took all three courses and 10 took none. How many took exactly two courses?
questions.exp: n(F∪M∪O) = 100 − 10 = 90. 90 = 60 + 45 + 45 − (sum of pairwise) + 10 → 90 = 160 − pairwise → pairwise = 70. Exactly two = 70 − 3 × 10 = 40.

questions.exp: Q — but the question is flawed. The stated clues are: P at the extreme left, S at the extreme right, and "Q is between P and R". With five seats, the clues allow several arrangements (P–Q–R–S–X, P–R–Q–S–X, etc.), so the middle seat is not uniquely determined. The intended arrangement is P–Q–R–S–(fifth), making Q third. Lesson: in the real hall, if a seating clue is genuinely ambiguous, answer the arrangement that satisfies all clues most naturally, and do not spend more than 60 seconds on it. One mark is not worth three.
